Portaria no. 551/GC3 of 9 August 2010, Art. 3, requires CENDOC to send originals to the Arquivo Nacional 'periodicamente', which is why the fund has no terminal year. b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: COMPARISON: a voluntary military transfer into a civil archive versus a statutory collection ordered by Congress
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no institutional contact between the Arquivo Nacional and NARA is claimed or evidenced. Brazil: from 2007 the Comando da Aeronáutica began sending its holdings to the Arquivo Nacional of its own motion, producing the Fundo Objeto Voador Não Identificado – OVNI (BR DFANBSB ARX), 743 registros, served online, with the service publicly disclaiming further competence. The United States: the UAP Records Collection in Record Group 615 exists only because sections 1841–1843 of Public Law 118-31 ordered it into being, with a statutory transfer deadline and with the independent review board stripped out in conference. Same archival endpoint, opposite mechanism — one service handed its record over, the other had to be legislated at. edges.label: COMPARISON: AARO's Foreign Partner Engagement section names no Latin American partner at all
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE, and a sourced negative. Section V.A of AARO's FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report is two sentences in full: 'During the reporting period, AARO continued to engage with international partners to exchange information and best practices for UAP reporting, analysis, and response. AARO's deputy director presented a mission briefing to the Defense Geospatial Intelligence conference in London, United Kingdom.' No foreign office, no foreign air force and no foreign archive is named anywhere in the document except that one London conference. Brazil, the FAB and the Arquivo Nacional — the largest declassified military UAP holding in the Americas — do not appear. The task asked what the section actually names: it names one conference in London and nothing else.

edges.label: The Brazilian Air Force mounted Operação Prato as its own field operation
edges.note: Operação Prato was run by the Força Aérea Brasileira out of the Belém air base in Pará, with the SNI, after mayors in the Colares area formally asked for help. The Brazilian Senate's own Requerimento 193/2022 lists it among the official Aeronáutica UAP programmes: 'Desde 1954, o Governo Brasileiro, por meio de sua Aeronáutica, já criou vários programas oficiais de pesquisas dos OVNIs, como em 1977, quando ocorreu a chamada Operação Prato'. Bob Pratt's file records that the operation was staffed by 'Captain Uyrangê Hollanda and six sergeants' and was shut down after four months by Brigadier Protázio Lopes de Oliveira, the base commander in Belém. This is the base institutional fact the whole Brazilian cluster hangs from and it was previously unwired. b.label: SETKA-AN / SETKA-MO (later Galaktika, then Gorizont) - Soviet state anomalous phenomena programme

edges.label: COMPARISON: two military UAP field-collection programmes that ended in publication rather than burial
edges.note: COMPARISON EDGE — no contact between the Brazilian and Soviet programmes is claimed or evidenced, and none is likely. The pairing is structural: Operação Prato was a small dedicated Air Force and SNI field detachment run under a military dictatorship that closed with an official negative finding and whose files later went to a civil national archive; SETKA was a thirteen-year standing collection tasking laid on the whole Soviet armed forces, written up afterwards by the men who ran it and published in the Academy of Sciences' own journal. Both are counter-examples to the US pattern in the same way and by opposite routes — one through an archive law, one through its own operators publishing. Brazil is named by a Peruvian government outlet as the regional benchmark. The same report establishes the office's identity that the peru-uap-office node lacked: the Departamento de Investigación de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (DIFAA), sitting under the Dirección de Intereses Aéreos Espaciales (DINAE), whose head Coronel FAP Julio Vucetich Abanto announced the public reporting channel, the office having been closed for five years 'a causa de problemas administrativos'. The reopening was announced at an FAP-hosted 'Encuentro sobre Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos' addressing the Nazca Lines question.
